- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect bearish sentiment’s fading.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% for the immediate follow-up days.
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion — if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to stay above; if below, stays below; adjust for smoother reversion toward historical mean.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum shifts; if sentiment flips sharply, adjust forecast 3–7 days ahead to reflect new sentiment direction.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply smoothing or weighted average of 3–5 prior days to reduce noise.
